questions.stem: Why is potassium more reactive than sodium?

options.text: Potassium has more electron shells, so its outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily
Potassium has more protons, which repel the outer electron more strongly
Potassium has a smaller atomic radius and stronger nuclear attraction
Potassium has fewer electron shells, so the outer electron is closer to the nucleus

questions.explanation: Potassium has more electron shells than sodium, meaning the outer electron is further from the nucleus. There is also more shielding from inner electrons. This makes the outer electron easier to lose, making potassium more reactive.
